decision.comment: Configuration replay is internally consistent and free of deterministic findings. Key verification points: (1) ResNet18 with hidden=48 correctly sets base channel width; depth=3 is inert per fixed-topology rule. (2) Transformer fields (num_heads, patch_size, mlp_ratio, tokenizer_layers, pooling, positional_encoding) are present but inactive for the CNN family and do not alter the model. (3) Augmentations hflip and rotate180 are built-in primitives requiring no extension approval; the empty approved_extensions list is consistent. (4) Split manifest sizes (89,996 / 10,004 / 7,180) match verified PathMNIST; augmented_train_size 269,988 = 89,996 × 3 is arithmetically correct. (5) Normalization stats are sourced from train only (train_stats_only: true), preventing leakage. (6) test_metrics_used is false in all artefacts; selection rule is validation-only. (7) The architecture-research anomaly (action=revise, severity=warning) contains only documentation-level LLM issues: a prior-art brief train-size typo (82,763 vs. verified 89,996), a truncated description field, a misattributed evidence quote, a null llm_model_digest, a redundant pending extension-gate entry for a built-in primitive, and a non-divisible head/hidden combination note. None of these are deterministic, none affect the replayed configuration, and none justify stopping. The ±10° rotation suggestion from the research stage is not present in the actual augmentation list, so no unapproved extension is in play. The OOD test set (CRC-VAL-HE-7K, separate clinical center) is correctly flagged; the OOD aggregate will be the arithmetic mean of per-severity AUROCs, not a pooled-sample AUROC. No critical or blocking issues identified. Proceed to the next stage.
issues: Prior-art brief cited 82,763 as PathMNIST train size; verified split manifest confirms 89,996. Documentation correction needed in the prior-art brief (non-blocking).
llm_model_digest is null for ollama/qwen3.8; exact model weights are not pinned, limiting full reproducibility verification of the architecture-research LLM output.

Architecture-research LLM issue: augmentation_regularization evidence quote addresses unlearning quality rather than classification regularization; the inference to hflip as a spatial regularizer is not directly supported by the cited passage. The actual configuration's use of hflip is independently justified as a built-in primitive.
Extension-gate entry 'hflip_pathology_safe' (pending_review) is redundant since hflip is a built-in augmentation primitive; recommend removing or clarifying to avoid confusion in downstream gates.

Transformer head-count range (4-6) with hidden-dim range (128-256) in the research stage includes non-divisible combinations (e.g., 256/6); if a transformer candidate is later selected, implementer must ensure heads evenly divide hidden dim. Not applicable to the current resnet18 selection.
